title: Rebuild ProximalBase as a minimal core: iterates, squared losses and lasso functions (#849)
body:
Implements milestone 0 of #849: reduces the full post-#848 package to **iterates + mathematical interface + squared losses + minimal lasso support**. This is a breaking development reduction, not a 0.6.0 release.

The active source is **17 Julia files / 333,106 bytes**, down from **52 / 1,649,968 bytes** (79.8% smaller). Retains SparseIterate, BlockIterate, SymmetricSparseIterate; value/gradient/prox and pure prox_block[!] extension hooks; LeastSquaresLoss, SqrNormL2, QuadraticFunction, scalar Squared; NormL1, Scaled, ZeroFunction, LinearFunction and retained cache invalidation. Both iterate executable syntax trees match frozen post-#848 source.

Group penalties, other GLMs/penalties/sets, general compositions, LMO, Hessian/Newton frameworks, spectral/nuclear functions, GPU kernels and their historical catalogs are archived. The full implementation, dependencies, tests, docs and benchmark provenance remain at `eff21b6d7d33c622313122f46c6ee71693c101ee`, verified archival branches/legacy/full, and annotated non-release tag `preservation/post-848-full-2026-11-10`. Archival refs remain unprotected; administrator protection was requested after API authentication was unavailable.

Validation at implementation commit `e272df3b87dcacb982b64b0e2124ca75cc50a966`:

- Linux/Julia 1.13.3: all 18 declared test files pass with bounds checking, including original retained storage/ridge regressions and independent numerical references.
- Strict exported-API documentation build, lasso and extension examples, precompilation, API/ambiguity checks and 102 frozen-baseline benchmark-reference probes pass.
- Separate reference suites: 12,832 assertions; 13,440 exceptional scalar/array-step configurations with zero baseline mismatches; 80 scaled custom-extension checks.
- Required CI runs current Julia 1.x on Linux only, preserving protected `PR required jobs` and `PR merge gate` checks. Tests, docs/examples and frozen benchmark references are mandatory.

Declaration audit was independently accepted before removal. [Audit, preservation and extraction records](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/tree/refactor/minimal-core/docs/audit/minimal-core-849) include exact dependencies and retired-resource inventory. Controlled performance verification is complete with context-sensitive flags and attribution limits preserved in the audit. The [fresh GPT-6.1 Sol/high review](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/pull/850#pullrequestreview-5854890534) reports no substantive blockers at final head `814de5cf833109bedd710404ced23eb566390d79`; [exact-head required CI](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/actions/runs/42974966998) is green. The [final acceptance report](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/pull/850#issuecomment-6789259824) records all gates and preservation checks.

No ProximalSolvers source/pin/branch/CI changes. After this merges, PS #234 advances its dependency and validates minimal lasso solvers in a separate integration PR. No release, history rewrite, force push or wholesale merge from legacy/full.
